plan: My value is $24. To maximize profit, bid slightly below my value to win while paying less. Assume others bid near their values. If I bid $23, I might win if others bid lower. If others bid higher, I lose nothing. If I win, I profit $24 minus the third-highest bid. This bid balances winning chances and minimizing payment.

Given my value of $9, I should bid conservatively. Other bidders likely value the item higher, and overbidding risks paying more than my value. I will bid slightly above the midpoint of my value to avoid overpayment while still having a chance to win if others bid low. This strategy minimizes potential loss and maintains a chance for profit if the third-highest bid is low.

Given my value of $13, I should bid close to my value to balance winning and profit. I anticipate others will bid near their values, so a bid slightly below $13 can secure the item if others bid lower. Bidding $12.5 maximizes profit if I win, as I pay the third-highest bid. If others bid above $13, I avoid loss. This strategy optimizes profit by considering the likelihood of winning versus the cost.
